column3: NASB reads “the testimony of God,” following other manuscripts; the critical text has “the mystery.” “Excellency” is rendered “superiority.”
NASB follows the critical text without “human.”
NASB adds “Yet … do” and renders “coming to naught” as “passing away.”
NASB renders “foreordained” as “predestined,” adds “the hidden wisdom,” and renders “for our glory” as “to our glory.”
The quotation is in capitals, with the supplied word “which”; “what” is rendered “ALL THAT.”
NASB follows the critical text (“For”) without “His”; it adds “them.”
NASB follows the critical text (“knows”); “the things” is rendered “the thoughts.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Holy”; it renders the last phrase as “combining spiritual thoughts with spiritual words,” though the meaning is uncertain.
NASB renders “judges” and “is judged” as “appraises” and “is appraised.”
The quotation is in capitals; “Who will instruct Him?” is rendered “THAT HE SHOULD INSTRUCT HIM?”
